lines.en: ERROR ADVANCING TO FRIDAY
Another day begins and, lo and behold, Imani storms into class and immediately usurps my role as “most important person in the room.”
But hey, she brought me coffee from the teacher’s lounge so, as far as I’m concerned, she can do whatever she wants for pretty much the rest of the day.

Sure, I imagined that we’d kind of ease into her intro instead of just letting her walk to the front of the room and start teaching a bunch of girls who have likely forgotten by now how school is supposed to work-

But it’s not like this changes my itinerary at all. In fact, it even takes some of the pressure off of me in that I can now hang out with the girls like I’m some sort of oversized, middle-aged high school student.
I hope the new teacher asks me to stay after class.
: Knowledge! Or, as I like to call it, the key to knowing stuff...is the third most important thing to fill your body with.
: The first of which is water, since us humans are comprised of roughly 75ish%% of it-
: And the second?
Imani pauses for dramatic effect, but everyone seems to be more confused than anything else.
: The second...
: Is friendship.
: Excuse me. I have a question.
: Yes! Ask me anything you’re curious about! I’m a repository of useful information!
: Pardon my language but, who the hell do you think you are?
: Woah there, Makoto! Ya can’t just go around askin’ teachers stuff like that! Not everybody’s as forgiving as Sensei is!
: We haven’t even confirmed if she’s an actual teacher yet. For all we know, she could be some random woman who just waltzed into class with a desire to try it out.
: But...I coulda sworn I heard ya talkin' about how she was the stand-in for Miss Watabe the other-
: Teaching’s no small task, Miku. It’s not something a person can just decide they want to do one day.
: Okay but like...do they have to decide that? Cause I feel like our normal teacher hasn’t even gotten to that point yet.
: Nonsense. Sensei just has unshakeable faith in me as a student and has decided to take the backseat in actual instructing so that I have more room to grow.
Oh, Makoto. I thought you were smarter than that.
: Hey, I get the frustration. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to figure out you might just think I’m some random woman who got lost and started scribbling things on a chalkboard.
: You didn’t even figure that out. You’re just paraphrasing what I said to my friend just now.
: What is your name, child?
: I’m not a child!
: What is your name, not-child?
: I’m...hah. Makoto Miyamura.
: Ahh, so you’re the one who was brought up at the maid cafe.
: Maid cafe? What are you talking about?
: What’s the issue here, Makoto? Is this more of a “Don’t interfere with how my favorite teacher does things” problem? Or a “You’re stealing my job” problem?
: It’s an “I don’t even know who you are” problem. I didn’t hear anything from Sensei or the principal about a new teacher, and I always hear about things like this before they happen.
: Apparently not! Because I’ve known about this all week and Sensei’s known about it for like, twelve hours or something.
: Are you a student teacher, then? Is that what’s going on?
: And, if that’s the case, shouldn’t you maybe...introduce yourself before telling us to put friendship into our bodies? Like, how would that even work?
: Yeah. I love Makoto, but I don’t really know how I feel about her gettin’ all up in my body, new teacher lady.
: To whom it may concern! Which...I guess is all of you.
: My name is Imani Imai and I’m going to be your new student teacher.
: You don’t have to call me Sensei or anything since that would probably get confusing really fast.
: In fact, you don’t even have to treat me like a teacher if you don’t want to! I’m of the belief that minds are better molded when done so on a casual, informal level.
: I’ve been sent here to keep you guys up to snuff on education stuff, while also keeping the school off of Sensei’s back for extremely understandable reasons!
: Are you getting fired, Sensei? Because this teacher just seems like a better, cuter version of you so far.
: I don’t know if I’d compare her to me just yet. But, at least from what I figured out yesterday, she’s not exactly an average teacher either.
: What do you mean?
: Well, the first time she came into my office, she accused Miss Watabe and me of “fucking” each other.
: Oh my god. Are you? Does Nodoka know?
: Wait, was Nodoka there? Did all three of you-
: No, Rin.
Not yet, at least.
: Why would...she assume something like that?
: Because she’s weird? I don’t know what you want me to say here.
: She’s already taken over the room and she’s only been here for five minutes. She’s clearly a force to be reckoned with.
: You just...seem to know her pretty well for...someone you just met...
: Hm.
: I guess that’s not entirely incorrect.
: I’m sure you’ll all be saying the same thing about her soon enough, though.
: Just look at Makoto, she’s already coming to terms with it.
: Listen! All I’m saying is that it’s not wrong for me to doubt the legitimacy of this without seeing your papers!
: Woah there! You already taking shots at my heritage, Makoto?! I’ll have you know I’m a legal citizen of Japan, thank you very much!
: Your assignment papers! I couldn’t care less about your citizenship paperwork!
: Which brings us right to today’s discussion- dual citizenship! Thank you, Makoto, for the excellent segue!
: It wasn’t a segue! And why is this your choice for a first lesson in our class?!
: So, now that we have an actual topic to go off of, how about we dive in a little deeper?
: I figure that just having one good discussion every morning is a much better way of getting you guys to learn stuff than forcing you to read textbooks and all that junk.
: Oooh! I’m sorry, Makoto, but I’m startin’ to like her! She’s speakin’ my language all of a sudden.
: So, dual citizenship...what is it?
: Well, just as the name implies, it’s when one person is registered as a legal citizen in two separate countries or states or- you know, basically, just two different places.
: But Japan is actually one of the few nations that doesn’t recognize dual citizenship.
: This means that mixed people like me are forced to choose one before we turn 22.
: So...does that mean you legally count as 100%% Japanese now? I don’t think I’m understanding the...legality of this rule.
: Great question and nice to meet you! What’s your name?
: Futaba...Fukuyama.
: Well, Futaba, I don’t blame you for not understanding the rules since they’re pretty inconsistent and nonsensical, but I’ll try to break down a few more aspects of it for you.
: I’m 100%% Japanese on a strictly legal basis because I was forced to surrender my Ghanaian nationality in order to count as a full citizen here.
: Well, forced probably isn’t the right word since it was something I chose to do, but still! Surrendering a nationality you’re born with is just one of several ways to legally become Japanese.
: Foreign adults can acquire that nationality by living in the country for over five years, whereas adopted children from foreign countries only have to live here for one.
: It works in reverse, too. For example, if I registered for dual citizenship in Ghana, a country that allows it, I would automatically lose my Japanese nationality despite being a current citizen.
: What a world we live in! Where the country we live in can just decide we’re not a real citizen anymore because we want to exist in two places at once.
: So! Do we have anyone else from mixed backgrounds here? Or am I just going to stick out even more than I already do?
: I’m kind of zoning out because this discussion is boring, but I just wanna say right now that I really want to fuck the new teacher.
: You want to fuck every teacher, Kirin.
: Well, I mean...not every teacher...
: Just...the two that are in this room.
: I’d probably be down to let Miss Watabe dom me too since I’ve heard she’s into that sort of thing.
: Wakana? Yeah, I can see that.
: Hey! How about we make a deal? You can get the new teacher and I can get Sensei!
: Then, when I’m no longer able to suppress the aggressive hormones raging inside of my body, we can have hot group sex every Friday night.
: Does it even count as “group sex” if it’s just two couples fucking each other in the same room?
: Is it a group of people?
: Yeah.
: Is there sex?
: Uhh, yeah.
: Well, then that should answer all of your questions.
: Okay! There’s the bell!
: Everybody get ready for gym class! Unless you’re too embarrassed to change in front of others or just...don’t want to or something!
: I don’t know! Do whatever it is you normally do when the real teacher is leading the class!
: I’m going to go find a burrito somewhere!
: Class dismissed!
Imani rushes out of the classroom and is quickly followed by a bunch of girls who still don’t understand if she’s really going to stick around or if this was just a long, elaborate joke.
One notable student does wind up sticking around after everyone else leaves, though.
: Maya? What’s up?
: Are you here to tell me some secret about another cycle coming to a close or something like that?
: No. I’m here to remind you of another Secret Santa exchange so you don’t wind up disappointing some other girl the way you disappointed me last Christmas.
: Wait, did I actually disappoint you?
: Of course. But you disappoint me every single day, so I didn’t think it was a particularly big deal.
: Well first off, I apologize for existing.
: It’s okay. I forgive you.
: Second, how do you know about this year’s Secret Santa? I thought everything happening was new to you now.
: Because it’s been written on the board for two weeks and you were asleep when we drew names.
: You’re not very observant, are you?
: Not about things I’m not particularly interested in, no.
: So, who do I have this year?
: Not a clue. But we shoved the only unclaimed slip of paper into your podium earlier this morning before our new...student teacher showed up?
: How do you feel about that, by the way?

: I feel as though I may be forced to actually learn something for the first time in a very, very long time. And I worry that my hands may no longer remember how to hold a pencil for any tests assigned to us.
: Well, you sure knew how to hold one when you filled a fake journal with information on yourself and all of your-
: I’m leaving now. I’ll see you later tonight.
: Wait, tonight?
: I’m sleeping over for the mini Christmas party we’re having at your house.
: How do you know about all of these things without secret knowledge from the future?
: Because I talk to people about things other than just sex and boobies.
: Anyway, bye.
: Make sure that whatever present you decide to buy for the person unfortunate enough to be assigned to you isn’t one that will get immediately tossed into the trash.
: Thanks, Maya. I’ll make sure to pick up a separate present for you too and-
: Okay. Good talk.
Huh.
Well, at least it’s not Maya this time.
But what the hell am I supposed to buy for Miku?
I don’t think it’ll be too hard since I know she likes...soccer and...running and stuff- but neither of those things sound like they’d make particularly exciting gifts.
Oh well.
I’ll probably just wait until the last minute and choose whatever I can find.
Or, if I’m really struggling, just get her a gift card or something.
I don’t care what anyone says about how gift cards are impersonal or bad gifts or anything.
Nothing says “I care about you” more than trusting someone with the free will to make their own decisions rather than making one for them, in my opinion.
But, this is clearly no time for an inner debate like that since I’m now acutely aware that someone else is standing in front of my desk.
: Surprise Ayane visit! Time to love me!
: You need to stop skipping gym class to come and see me. People are going to realize what your game is.
: Everyone’s known my game since the start, Sensei! I’m like the Ami that people won’t think is weird for liking you so much since you and me aren’t actually related.
: So, what’s up then? If this is about the Secret Santa thing, Maya just reminded me.
: Well...it’s not about that. But it is kind of a present, I guess?
: I just wanted to give you a sneak peek of something so I could get your thoughts on it before everyone else sees it.
: Plus, we haven’t really been spending any time in school alone lately and...yeah.
: It’s kind of hard to find alone time when I’m surrounded by an ever-increasing number of girls.
: So, what is it you wanted to show me?
: Well, I’m not going to just tell you! That would ruin the surprise!
: You’ll have to follow me if you want to see it!
: Then...lead the way, I guess?
: Oh, Io. What’s up? Hiding from the rest of the girls again?
: Something like that...
: Did you need something?
: Yeah, but I’m trying to figure out how to say it in a way that doesn’t sound annoying or cringeworthy or like...lame? Weird? I don’t know.
: Well you’re already off to a rocky start, but that’s basically what I’ve come to expect from you by now.
: Okay, so...hypothetically, if a girl that liked you made you a Christmas present and wanted to give it to you, would you rather she be honest about it? Or would that come off as like...overbearing?
: If this is about me coming over to see what you made for me after school, I already planned on it.
: What? How did you know about that?
: Uta told me yesterday when I went to the maid cafe with Imani and Wakana.
: Was she...not supposed to do that?
: Uta did?...Huh. That’s weird.
If I’m remembering correctly, I’m pretty sure Uta said that Io asked her to tell me about it, too- which I’m suddenly realizing was probably not the case.
: So...Uta aside, you’ll come then?
: I will.
: And you won’t think I went way overboard when you see what I made?
: Well...I mean, that kind of depends.
: I’m sure that as long as I can carry it home, whatever you made will be fine.
: And if you can’t carry it home?
: Io, what did you make me?
: A-Anyway! See you later! And remember that you can always regift stuff if you don’t like it and I won’t blame you at all since I definitely went way overboard!
: Io, what did you-
: Nothing! Bye!
Well, looks like my first Christmas present of the year might wind up being a little more than I bargained for.
Which, need I remind you, was absolutely nothing.
But hey, if Io wants to bust her ass making some sort of crazy gift for me, she can feel free.
Here’s hoping that it provided at least some sort of distraction for her.
And here’s hoping that I didn’t accidentally get Uta in trouble by revealing I knew about this gift from the get go.
